lines.label: of which: from the two businesses combined at the end of Quarter 4

text_lines.fact: Agreed to combine with two Asian facility businesses, issuing ~93.7m and ~76.6m shares (27.5% and 22.5% of the fully diluted company), plus $30-40m of secured convertible notes at ~$0.34 a share; bondholders to swap for cash and shares
If the combination fails the company will most likely seek bankruptcy protection
Lenders waived the bond-conversion deadline and a missed December bond interest payment, pending the deal
Holders of $103.7m of bonds have offered to tender

The combination and financing closed on the last day of the quarter: two similar businesses joined, a 30.0m convertible secured note was issued to the larger partner's parent, and 116.8m of bonds were retired for about 1.9m new shares and 15.2m cash. A 1-for-32 reverse share split was done to keep the stock listed.
Bank covenants reset in December to match the combined company's plan.
In compliance with all debt covenants. A breach would still require repaying about 91.5m the company does not have.
Management says cash on hand, operating cash from the second half of the year and combination savings cover the next twelve months.

Excluding the combined businesses, revenue was flat year on year (20.3m vs 20.2m), but recurring revenue rose 17%; the drop was in one-off items (settlement fees and equipment resale a year earlier). Resizing of large customers' contracts was complete by December.
A venture investor put in 10.0m of new convertible secured notes; warrants exercised.
Recurring revenue in the main market up 46% year on year; customer count there 428 against 248 a year earlier (includes two acquired sites).
Still in compliance with all covenants, now including a monthly minimum cash balance.

basis_notes: Each quarter is shown as reported at the time. From Quarter 5 the company includes two businesses it combined with on the last day of Quarter 4; Quarter 5 and 6 revenue therefore includes about 5.1m a quarter from them.
Quarter 4 has no separate quarterly report. Its figures are the annual report totals less the first three quarters; the annual report rounds to 0.1m, so Quarter 4 figures carry that rounding.
Depreciation in Quarter 6 includes a small new accretion charge required by an accounting change that year.
The Quarter 3 report was later amended (10-Q/A); the statement figures used here match both versions.

outcome.fact: The company never filed for bankruptcy. The rescue closed on 31 December 2002; the bonds were swapped for shares and cash at a steep discount, booking a 114.2m gain in 2002.

outcome.fact: The parent of one combined business became the largest shareholder and lender.
By early 2024 the company reported more than 8bn of annual revenue and 21 years of consecutive quarterly revenue growth, a run that begins almost exactly where this reveal ends.
The Case A company appears in this company's filings among customers that went bankrupt.
